name: Stop Slop
short_description: Strip the phrases and rhythms that mark writing as AI-generated so drafts read like a person wrote them. It rewrites against concrete banned-pattern rules and scores the result for human voice.
install_command: Install this skill collection or give me an instruction how to install it: https://github.com/hardikpandya/stop-slop
long_description:
Stop Slop teaches your agent to catch and remove the patterns that mark writing as AI-generated. It rewrites prose against concrete rules: banned phrases and throat-clearing openers, structural cliches like binary contrasts and dramatic fragmentation, and sentence-level bans on em dashes and staccato fragments.

Then it scores the result from 1 to 10 on five dimensions of human voice: directness, rhythm, trust, authenticity, and density. Anything below the threshold gets another pass. Add it as a skill in Claude Code or any LLM that reads the SKILL.md format.

when_to_use.body: It rewrites against concrete banned-pattern rules so drafts read like a person wrote them.
when_to_use.title: Your writing has that AI smell

when_to_use.body: It grades the result so you can tell whether the slop is actually gone.
when_to_use.title: You want a human-voice score before publishing

faq.a: Stop Slop rewrites against concrete banned-pattern rules covering throat-clearing openers, em dashes, and business jargon, then scores the result out of 10 for human voice rather than relying on a vague instruction.
faq.q: How is Stop Slop different from just asking the model to sound human?

faq.a: Stop Slop is a single Markdown skill. You add the folder as a skill in Claude Code, upload SKILL.md to a Claude Project, or include it in your API system prompt so the reference files load on demand.
faq.q: How do I use Stop Slop?

faq.a: Yes. Stop Slop is open-source under the MIT license with no paid tier, and it runs inside whatever model or agent you already use.
faq.q: Is Stop Slop free?
